source.extractionNote: One set (2 variants, no children inside either) and a full 'Scrim Metadata' frame read in full. No subcomponents.

summary: The translucent barrier between a raised surface and the page behind it. Dialog, Lightbox and Bottom Sheet draw it under their panels: it dims everything behind, keeps the page from being read as interactive, and catches the click that dismisses. It is one fill stretched edge to edge — overlay/scrim — with an opaque modal tone (overlay/modal) for a full takeover. It has no content, no shape and no motion of its own; the owning component carries all three.

intent.scrim: The translucent barrier — overlay/scrim, the fill every backdrop in the system uses. Content behind stays visible but reads as unavailable.
intent.modal: The opaque takeover — overlay/modal, for the rare surface where the page behind must not show at all. It cannot serve as a see-through backdrop.

anatomy.role: 1. Barrier — The whole component: one rectangle, fill bound to overlay/scrim (or overlay/modal), stretched over the owning surface’s viewport. No children, no stroke, no radius, no shadow — everything else on screen belongs to the surface above or the page below.

themeAxes.extensions: every brand extension in tokens/manifest.json resolves the two overlay tokens

table.What changes: Appears with its owner — the scrim defines no timing of its own; the owner’s entry carries it.

table.Trigger: Click or tap on the scrim
table.What changes: Dismisses the owner when the owner is dismissible. The scrim only forwards the event; it decides nothing itself.
Leaves with the owner; nothing lingers.

table.Description: The scrim belongs to the component it sits under. Dialog, Lightbox and Bottom Sheet draw it as their native backdrop bound to overlay/scrim — it is never placed by hand over a page, and a product never opens a bare scrim.
One scrim per open surface, ordered by the native top layer. Never draw a second scrim to darken further: one overlay/scrim is the system’s entire dimming scale.
A click on the scrim closes the owner only when the owner allows it (dismissible); Escape is the keyboard parity, handled by the owner. The scrim never closes anything on its own.
None of its own. No motion token exists for a fade, and the owner’s entry carries the scrim with it — in code the backdrop simply appears with the dialog.
A scrim carries nothing. Anything readable or interactive sits on the raised surface above it, never on the barrier itself.

do: Let the owning component draw the scrim — Dialog, Lightbox and Bottom Sheet already do — so there is exactly one per open surface and it leaves when the surface does.
Dim with the scrim tone. Reserve modal for a takeover where the page behind must not read at all — a first-run flow, not an everyday dialog.
dont: Don’t stack scrims or darken one with an opacity override. One overlay/scrim is the system’s entire dimming scale, in every mode and extension.
Don’t put text or controls on the scrim. It makes no contrast promise against what is behind it, so nothing on it is reliably readable.

accessibility: The scrim is decorative: never focusable, never named — the owning dialog traps focus and makes the page behind inert.
Dismissing by clicking the scrim always has keyboard parity: Escape on the owner.
The scrim makes no contrast promise for the content behind it; nothing that must stay readable may rely on showing through.
overlay/scrim and overlay/modal are semantic tokens, so the barrier holds its role in light, dark and every brand extension.

table.Description: Edge to edge over the owning surface’s viewport — the native backdrop in code, stretch constraints in a layout. Never a fixed size; the 640×400 variants are drawing surfaces.
overlay/scrim for the translucent tone, overlay/modal for the opaque takeover. Both semantic; nothing hardcodes a colour.
radius/none — the scrim has no shape of its own.
No shadow. The raised surface above carries the elevation; the scrim is what it is raised above.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: Tone=scrim adds a paint-level opacity of 0.6 on top of overlay/scrim, which already carries its own alpha (primitives alpha/dark/60). Figma therefore draws a lighter dim than the token, and the metadata says never to darken or lighten with an opacity override. Implement the token alone, with no extra opacity.

palette fill/scrim's description says the alias is fully opaque and opacity is applied at usage, but it aliases a translucent alpha primitive. The stale description is the likely cause of the paint opacity above.
The set description says Scrim has no code element. In code, Dialog, Lightbox and a modal Bottom Sheet render the Scrim component as their backdrop.
The Default column's icon marks scrim as the default, matching Figma's default variant.
Motion is none by intent: no fade token exists and the owner carries the entry. The 640×400 size is a Figma drawing surface, not a size to implement.
